title: Post Processor Foundation — Pipeline Orchestrator + Input Normalization
description: Build the core PostProcessorPipelineEngine that orchestrates 35+ optimization stages across 7 phases. Create the input normalization layer that accepts G-code, CL data, toolpath JSON, or Fusion CPS context and converts to a unified ToolpathBlock[] internal representation. Build the smart defaults system that fills missing parameters from PRISM's catalogs (910 machines, 46,590 tools, 2,957 materials, 1,164 holders). This milestone is the backbone — every subsequent PP milestone plugs stages into this pipeline.

units.title: Create PostProcessorPipelineEngine skeleton with stage registry, phase ordering, and configurable stage enable/disable
steps: Define PipelineStage interface: { id, phase, order, name, engine, enabled, run(context) → context }
Define PipelineContext type: carries all state between stages (blocks, tools, machine, material, metrics, warnings)
Create PostProcessorPipelineEngine with registerStage(), runPipeline(), getStageReport() methods
Implement phase ordering: P0-INPUT → P1-PHYSICS → P2-BLOCKOPT → P3-MOTION → P4-STOCHASTIC → P5-SAFETY → P6-OUTPUT
Implement stage dependency resolution — stages can declare dependencies on other stages
Implement stage skip logic — if input lacks data for a stage, skip gracefully with warning
Add pipeline timing — track ms per stage for performance profiling
Add pipeline event emitter — progress callbacks for UI integration
exit_conditions: PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts compiles with 0 errors
Empty pipeline runs and returns empty context
Stages execute in declared phase/order sequence
Disabled stages are skipped
Stage timing is reported in pipeline result

units.title: Create PipelineContext type system — the universal data contract between all stages
steps: Define ToolpathBlock: { id, type (rapid/linear/arc/drill/tap/probe), x/y/z/a/b/c, i/j/k/r, feed, speed, tool_number, engagement?: { ae, ap, theta, d_eff }, forces?: { Fc, Ff, Fp }, thermal?: { T_tool, T_chip, cumulative_heat }, wear?: { VB, VB_rate }, confidence?: { feed_ci, force_ci } }
Define MachineContext: resolved from catalog — spindle curve, axis limits, rapid rates, accel/jerk, controller type, controller version, kinematics, work volume, tool changer type/time
Define ToolContext: resolved from catalog — geometry (D, L, flute_count, helix, corner_r), grade, kc1_1, mc, max_Vc, coating, stiffness, runout_TIR
Define HolderContext: resolved from catalog — type, taper, gauge_length, stiffness, max_RPM, balance_grade
Define MaterialContext: resolved from DB — ISO group, UTS, hardness, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, constitutive_model_params (JC/ZA coefficients)
Define CoolantContext: type (flood/mist/MQL/cryo/dry), pressure, flow_rate, nozzle_count
Define PipelineResult: { blocks: ToolpathBlock[], gcode: string, analytics: AnalyticsReport, setup_sheet: SetupSheet, warnings: Warning[], stage_timings: Map<string,number> }
exit_conditions: All context types defined with Zod schemas
Types are exported and importable by all engine stages
PipelineContext can carry full state from Stage 0.1 through Stage 6.7

units.title: Stage 0.1 — Input parser: G-code → ToolpathBlock[], CL data → ToolpathBlock[], toolpath JSON → ToolpathBlock[]
steps: G-code parser: handle G0/G1/G2/G3, canned cycles (G81-G89), tool changes (T/M6), spindle (S/M3/M4/M5), coolant (M7/M8/M9), work offsets (G54-G59), sub-programs (M98/M99)
CL data parser: parse APT/CL format — GOTO, CIRCLE, FEDRAT, SPINDL, COOLNT, TURRET, TLDATA
Toolpath JSON parser: accept PRISM's native { blocks: [...] } format from MCP interface
Fusion CPS context parser: accept enriched JSON sidecar from Fusion .cps post (tool list, operations, stock, WCS)
All parsers produce identical ToolpathBlock[] output — unified internal representation
Auto-detect input format from content inspection (G-code vs CL vs JSON)
exit_conditions: G-code with 100+ lines parses correctly to ToolpathBlock[]
CL data with GOTO/CIRCLE/FEDRAT parses correctly
JSON passthrough works
Format auto-detection works for all 4 formats
15+ unit tests covering parser edge cases

units.title: Stage 0.2-0.5 — Context resolution: Machine + Tool + Holder + Material from catalogs
steps: Machine resolver: match user input (name/model/brand) → MachineContext from 910-machine catalog. Fuzzy match. Extract spindle curve, axis limits, rapid rates, controller type
Tool resolver: match user input (description/catalog_id/dimensions) → ToolContext from 46,590-tool catalog. Exact match by ID or fuzzy by geometry
Holder resolver: match user input or auto-select best holder for tool+machine taper from 1,164-holder catalog. Calculate assembly stiffness
Material resolver: match user input (name/grade/UNS/ISO) → MaterialContext from 2,957-material DB. Extract constitutive model params
Each resolver returns confidence score (exact_match=1.0, fuzzy=0.5-0.9, default=0.3)
Log all resolution decisions for traceability
exit_conditions: Machine 'DMG MORI DMU 50' resolves to correct catalog entry with spindle curve
Tool 'OSG AE-VMS-10' resolves to exact catalog entry with kc1.1/mc
Material '316L stainless' resolves with JC constitutive params
Fuzzy matching handles abbreviations and common variants
12+ unit tests

units.title: Stage 0.6-0.7 — Smart defaults + Transfer learning for missing inputs
steps: Smart defaults engine: fill ALL gaps when user provides minimal input
Missing material → infer from operation context or use generic '4140 steel' with warning
Missing machine → select best-fit from catalog based on part envelope + operation types
Missing tool → auto-select from ToolSelectionEngine based on operation + material + dimensions
Missing holder → auto-select for maximum stiffness at required reach
Missing coolant → derive from material ISO group + operation type + playbook rules
Missing tolerance → ISO 2768-m (medium) for general, ISO 2768-f (fine) for finishing ops
Missing surface finish → Ra 3.2 roughing, Ra 1.6 semi-finish, Ra 0.8 finishing, Ra 0.4 superfinish
Aggressiveness slider: 0.0 (first article / unknown setup) → 1.0 (proven setup / max productivity). Default 0.5
Transfer learning integration: query TransferLearningEngine for similar past setups → parameter priors with confidence
All defaults logged with reasoning for user review
exit_conditions: Pipeline runs with ONLY material='aluminum' and operation='roughing' — fills everything else
Aggressiveness=0.3 produces measurably more conservative S/F than 0.7
Transfer learning priors override generic defaults when confidence > 0.6
15+ unit tests for default selection logic

units.title: Wire PostProcessorPipelineEngine to camDispatcher with pipeline actions
steps: Create postProcessorPipelineActionSchemas.ts with Zod schemas for pipeline actions
Action: pp_run_full — run complete pipeline (all stages)
Action: pp_run_partial — run specific phase range (e.g., Phase 2-5 only for re-optimization)
Action: pp_analyze — dry run, return analytics without generating G-code
Action: pp_configure — set stage enable/disable, aggressiveness, output format
Action: pp_resolve_context — run Phase 0 only, return resolved machine/tool/material/holder context
Wire all actions to camDispatcher with lazy loading
Create integration test: full pipeline from G-code input → optimized G-code output
exit_conditions: All 5 actions callable through camDispatcher
pp_run_full produces optimized G-code from raw G-code input
pp_run_partial works for Phase B (re-optimization) scenario
pp_analyze returns force/thermal/time/cost predictions without codegen
Build: 0 errors. 20+ tests
